Russian attacks injure four people in the Dnipropetrovsk region over the course of a day, with the region struck nearly 50 times, regional authorities say.

Russia attacked overnight with one Kh-59 guided missile and 121 Shahed-type attack, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, the Ukrainian Air Force Command says; air defences shot down or suppressed 96 drones and the missile did not reach its target, with hits recorded at 11 locations. Ukrainian military claim.
Ukraine's General Staff reports 225 combat clashes over the past 24 hours, the most in the Pokrovsk sector, alongside 91 Russian airstrikes dropping 288 guided bombs. Ukrainian military claim.
Two people were killed and three injured as Russian forces carried out 923 strikes on the Zaporizhzhia region over the past day, regional authorities say. Ukrainian regional claim.

A missile attack on the Russian city of Belgorod killed two people and injured 16, acting governor Alexander Shuvayev says, after a Ukrainian strike on a commercial facility set seven warehouses ablaze; Russian retailer Ozon says a logistics hub and a sorting facility were hit. Russian official claim.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Belgorod acting governor, Ozon)

timeline.event: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says NATO's moves in the Arctic pose a "direct threat" to Russia; NATO said separately it sees no imminent threat of attack.

Russian drone attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region stretch into a fifth day, with near round-the-clock air raid sirens disrupting daily life; attacks early on Monday injure four people and damage warehouses, an apartment block and a retail outlet, regional governor Tymur Tkachenko says. Ukrainian official account.

Six people are injured in drone attacks on Kyiv and the village of Pohreby, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says; three are hospitalised in serious condition and warehouse facilities in Pohreby catch fire. Ukrainian official claim.

Energy company DTEK says Russian forces have attacked its Dnipropetrovsk region facilities three times in recent days; power was restored to 40,000 customers over two days but another 30,000 remain without electricity. Company statement.
Ukraine's Defence Forces say they struck a Russian radar, an S-400 command-and-staff vehicle and supply depots. Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the oil tanker MV Sun, suspected of sailing under a false flag, was boarded on 30 August in the Mediterranean by EUNAVFOR MED IRINI forces for flag verification — the sixth suspected Russian shadow-fleet vessel boarded by EU operations in recent months. Shadow-fleet action is on the agenda when EU defence ministers meet in Ireland on Tuesday.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pledges a "swift response" to Russian hybrid attacks; separately, Polish authorities are investigating possible sabotage after a fire at a Polish drone manufacturer.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 173 combat clashes along the front on 31 August, with 66 Russian airstrikes dropping 218 guided glide bombs, 6,542 kamikaze drones deployed and 2,049 attacks on settlements and positions. The heaviest fighting was again in the Pokrovsk sector, where 32 assaults were repelled and, by preliminary Ukrainian estimates, 53 Russian troops were killed and 18 wounded. Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

The Kherson Regional Prosecutor's Office says three civilians were killed and seven injured, including an 11-year-old boy, in Russian artillery and drone attacks across the region during the day. A 65-year-old woman in Kostyrka was killed by a drone strike; a Russian drone also hit a supermarket roof in Kherson, injuring a child. War-crimes investigations have been opened. Ukrainian official account.

The Kyiv Regional Military Administration says nine people were injured in Russian air attacks in the Kyiv region during the day, eight of them in the village of Pohreby, with warehouses damaged in three districts and two houses damaged in Bucha district. Ukrainian official account.

Polish prosecutors open a terrorism investigation into a fire at the WB Electronics drone factory in Skarzysko-Kamienna, saying it was started deliberately with a device containing flammable materials, and also investigating “participation in the activities of a foreign intelligence service directed against the Republic of Poland”. No suspect has been named; Poland has repeatedly accused Russia of sabotage since 2022 and Moscow has denied it.

Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attends a G20 finance ministers' meeting in Asheville, North Carolina in person — his first since the 2022 invasion — after a US invitation, and holds a bilateral meeting with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that a US official says focused on President Trump's Ukraine peace plan. German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil calls the presence a “quite troubling” signal and says Europe is preparing a further sanctions package; European officials refuse to appear in the family photo, which is taken without Siluanov.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (G20 delegations, German finance ministry, US Treasury)

timeline.event: Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping hold talks in Bishkek as the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit opens. Xi says Russia–China ties have become “more solid”; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says the pair discussed the Ukraine war only “in passing”.

Russian strikes have destroyed some 12 million books as Ukraine returns to school, the BBC reports, after missiles hit publishing warehouses, printing presses nationwide and a well-known second-hand book market in Kyiv. One plant on the edge of Kyiv was hit overnight as it ramped up to deliver 1.3 million books — about 10 per cent of Ukraine's schoolbooks.
Debris from Russian drones falls in two districts of Kyiv overnight, sparking fires, according to Ukrainian authorities.

Nine people are killed and more than a dozen injured in Russian air attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region, the sixth consecutive day of strikes on the capital, Ukrainian authorities say. The State Emergency Service says eight were killed and five wounded in Kyiv itself, three of them children, with fires in several districts; in Boryspil, Kyiv regional governor Tymur Tkachenko says one person was killed and nine injured, including a child, after missiles and drones damaged an apartment building and a business facility. Air raid alerts covered most of Ukraine in the early hours. The figures are Ukrainian officials' account; Moscow has not commented.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Ukrainian State Emergency Service, Kyiv regional administration)

timeline.event: A fresh Russian strike halts border crossings into Romania, a member of the EU and NATO, at Orlivka on the Danube, CNA reports, as Russia widens attacks on Ukraine's borders alongside energy and logistics facilities. Separately, CNA reports a drone attack caused a fire in the port area of Ust-Luga, a major Russian export outlet in the north-west.

Ukraine's sanctions commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk is in Washington to lobby members of the US House to back the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which passed the Senate with bipartisan support but faces opposition in the House over its tariff powers and political risk ahead of the midterms. If enacted it would let the president impose steep tariffs on countries dependent on Russian energy, with discretion to lift them.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Vladyslav Vlasiuk, via Reuters interview)

timeline.event: Ukraine's air force says air defences neutralised 10 missiles and 187 drones in the overnight attack, and a spokesperson says all cruise missiles launched at Ukraine were shot down. The tallies are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified.

The toll from the overnight strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region rises to at least 12 killed and 20 injured, including two children, Ukrainian officials say. Eight died in Kyiv — six of them workers at a state railway depot hit in the city — and four in Boryspil, where a residential building was struck. President Volodymyr Zelensky said nearly 350 rescue workers were deployed overnight. Russia's defence ministry said its “massive strike using high-precision weapons” targeted Ukrainian military and energy facilities and said one person was killed by Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Belgorod region. All figures are the claims of parties to the war.

Russia attacks port export infrastructure in the Odesa region and damages the Orlivka ferry checkpoint on the Romanian border — the fourth strike on that crossing, Ukraine's border service says — suspending processing of people and vehicles. Zelensky said the strike “deliberately damaged a border crossing point on the border with Romania, as well as export infrastructure”; the emergency service said energy infrastructure was also targeted and one person was hurt in a fire at a residential building. Odesa recorded more than 300 air-raid alerts in August, lasting a combined 238 hours, according to a monitoring service.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, Ukrinform (Zelensky, State Border Guard Service)

timeline.event: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly urges Vladimir Putin at a regional security summit in Kyrgyzstan to end the war, saying “every day spent in war pushes humanity back”. India buys heavily discounted Russian oil and has stayed broadly neutral; BBC correspondents read the remarks as continuity rather than a policy shift.

Ukraine's General Staff says Russian forces lost more than 124,000 troops over the summer, about 25 per cent more than in spring, and another 1,440 personnel in the past 24 hours. These are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified; Russia does not publish comparable figures.
Ukraine's parliament fails to pass a parcel tax law tied to IMF and EU funding, leaving a condition of external financing unmet.

Ukraine's military intelligence directorate (DIU) says its operators, in a joint deep-strike operation with Ukrainian Defence Forces, hit the Novatek-Ust-Luga complex in Russia's Leningrad region overnight, reporting damage to key refinery components and a large fire. This is a Ukrainian military claim and has not been independently verified; Russian authorities have not confirmed the damage.

Ukraine's Air Force Command says Russia launched 99 strike drones between 06:30 and 18:00 on 1 September, 72 of them jet-powered, and that air defences shot down or suppressed 82 of them, 57 jet-powered. It says around 10 jet-powered drones were still in Ukrainian airspace at 18:30 with new groups entering. These are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified.

Zelensky warns airlines that Russian airspace is becoming dangerous, saying Ukrainian drones have effectively closed it, and threatens to keep it that way through mass drone deployment. Putin later says Russia would respond if Ukraine closes Russian airspace to commercial flights.

Germany says Russia was behind the 4 August drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport, where an explosive-carrying drone was found near Ukrainian cargo planes and failed to detonate. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says equipment analysis and intelligence proved Russian involvement; Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul orders the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, terminates the Russian House Berlin contract, tightens entry controls for Russian nationals and summons Moscow's ambassador. Russia's embassy calls the allegation 'absurd' and an 'unprecedented escalation', and foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova says Moscow will respond in 'mirror-image' fashion.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (German interior and foreign ministries, Russian embassy)

timeline.event: Explosives are used in a sabotage attack on power lines at a Brandenburg substation in Germany, with rockets carrying conductive material triggering short circuits. Grid operator 50Hertz says general electricity supply was unaffected. No party has been formally blamed.

Putin, speaking to reporters after the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, says Ukraine's 40-day strike campaign caused damage of about 1 per cent of Russia's GDP - 'real damage' but 'not critical' - and claims Ukraine damaged about 100 Russian ships, roughly 40 of them in the first two weeks. He says only about 10 per cent of Russia's refineries are still to be repaired, and separately says Russia is winning on the battlefield and will not negotiate with 'terrorists'. These are Russian presidential claims; Ukraine has not confirmed the figures.

Russian drones strike the Brovary and Bucha districts of the Kyiv region overnight, the regional administration says: a woman born in 1971 is hospitalised with a thigh wound in Brovary, and warehouse facilities are damaged and burning in Bucha. Regional head Tymur Tkachenko says drone attacks on the region have now run six days.

Russia's embassy in Germany calls Berlin's attribution of the Leipzig/Halle airport drone attack to Moscow an 'absurd and baseless provocation' and an unprecedented escalation, saying it benefits Ukraine and arms makers.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Russian embassy in Germany)

timeline.event: Putin responds to Zelensky's airspace warning by calling it 'a declaration of state terrorism', says Russia will continue its attacks and that its military is preparing 'massive' strikes on Ukrainian power stations, and acknowledges Ukrainian strikes damaged Russian infrastructure while insisting 'only 10%' of oil refineries are left to repair.

Aviation risk firm Osprey Flight Solutions tells clients that while most Ukrainian drone and missile strikes are likely to fall within 300km of the border, daily attacks deeper inside Russia are almost certain to continue this year, and that misidentification in the conflict zone is likely.
Putin says Ukraine's 40-day strike campaign, which began in June, damaged about 100 Russian ships, and repeats that Russia is winning on the battlefield and will not negotiate with 'terrorists'.

German police say they are investigating a second sabotage attack on the country's electricity grid, at a substation near Bergheim in the west, a day after explosives were used against power lines at a Brandenburg substation.

Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov says dialogue between Russia and the United States should continue to find common ground in economics, which he argues would make political discussions easier, according to Interfax. Canada's finance minister says Siluanov's presence at the G-20 'created discomfort'.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Interfax, Anton Siluanov, Canadian finance ministry)

timeline.event: Mykhailo Fedorov says Palantir chief executive Alex Karp will be the first major investor in his new defence company, and Ukrainian experts are to advise European governments on plugging their defence gaps.
The Kremlin says Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin may hold a trilateral meeting at the next APEC summit.

Russian drones tear into central Kyiv on the seventh day of near round-the-clock attacks, wounding nine people and damaging residential and university buildings. Zelensky says about 160 students had to shelter during a strike on a downtown university while classes were in progress.

Russian missiles and drones hit power facilities in the Odesa region, knocking out electricity to more than 350,000 homes, while two people are killed and eight wounded in Dnipro, where food warehouses and educational buildings were damaged, the regional governor says.

Ursula von der Leyen says the EU will increase pressure on Russia, including with new sanctions, after the Leipzig/Halle airport drone plot; Kaja Kallas says the attack had the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism and that measures are being prepared against Russia's military-industrial complex. Germany says it will close Russia's consulate general in Bonn and terminate its agreement with the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin, and the EU and several member states summon Russian embassy officials. Russia denies involvement.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte says more drones and missiles have crossed into alliance airspace on the eastern flank and that malign activity, including the Leipzig attack, is increasing.
Zelensky tells airlines, insurers and anyone using Russian airports that Russian skies are not safe, because Ukrainian drone operations over Russia are being scaled up.
Merchant ships in the Black Sea are fitting makeshift anti-drone defences as attacks on shipping intensify.
German officials say a test of an Israeli-made ballistic missile was successful, part of Berlin's build-out of layered air defence.

Ukraine formally notifies the International Civil Aviation Organization that Russian airspace is not safe for civil aviation, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha says, after Zelensky told airlines and insurers that 'the Russian sky is becoming completely dangerous'. Putin calls the warning a 'declaration of state terrorism'. FlightRadar24 still showed aircraft over Russia on Wednesday afternoon.
timeline.source: BBC (Andrii Sybiha, Volodymyr Zelensky, Vladimir Putin)

timeline.event: ICAO reiterates calls for stronger commitments to protect civilian aircraft from risks arising in conflict zones, responding to Ukraine's notification.

Ursula von der Leyen says 'Leipzig marks a new escalation on European Union soil directly attributed to Russia' and that the EU must respond 'faster and better'; Mark Rutte says NATO stands in full solidarity with Germany. Germany's interior minister says the drone's configuration, components, explosives and detonator are all known from other Russian hybrid operations, and two suspects have reportedly been identified, including a Belarusian holding a Russian passport who entered on a tourist visa. Russia rejects the German accusation.
timeline.source: BBC (Ursula von der Leyen, Mark Rutte, German interior ministry)

timeline.event: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blames high energy prices on Ukraine's strikes inside Russia; The Straits Times describes the remarks as consistent with the administration's willingness to pressure Kyiv while courting Moscow.

Norway seizes the Russian-owned vessel Professor Molchanov off Svalbard after a 24-hour standoff with its coast guard, to enforce a US$4.22 billion award won by Ukraine's Naftogaz over Russia's expropriation of its Crimean assets. A Hague tribunal ordered the payment in April 2023 and Moscow has not complied. Russia's foreign ministry, quoted by TASS, calls the seizure 'piracy'.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia will close Germany's Goethe-Institut cultural centres in Moscow, St Petersburg and Yekaterinburg, retaliating for Berlin's closure of a Russian cultural centre in Berlin and a consulate in Bonn over the Leipzig drone incident. Lavrov says further measures will follow. Putin said on 1 September that Germany planted the evidence.

EU foreign ministers meeting in Ireland summon Russia's envoys and discuss sanctions on some 1,600 Russian individuals and entities, plus a possible visa ban on Russians involved in the war. Foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the Leipzig incident has 'all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism'. Germany says it has identified two suspects. Russia denies involvement.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (Kaja Kallas, German government)

timeline.event: Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service says it has documents on at least eight Indonesian citizens recruited into Russia's army under false promises of high-paying jobs, publishing Russian visa and migration papers. Indonesia's foreign ministry says it must verify their identities, citizenship and the nature of their involvement; a deputy speaker of parliament confirmed on 1 September that the information had been shared. Russia has not commented.
timeline.source: CNA (Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine, Indonesian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: Britain summons Russia's charge d'affaires to condemn last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport, after the German government said Russia was responsible. Moscow denies involvement.

President Vladimir Putin says there is a chance of a peace settlement and that several countries, including the United States and China, are ready to support one, while arguing that Ukraine's warning to airlines about Russian airspace makes a deal harder; Kyiv says it sees a 'new dynamic'. No terms have been published and both characterisations come from parties to the war.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian officials)

timeline.event: Russia's Transport Ministry says it has given foreign airlines clarifications about the safety measures at Russian airports and in Russian airspace, after Volodymyr Zelensky warned carriers that flying over Russia had become unsafe.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Russian Transport Ministry, via Interfax)

timeline.event: German police investigate a suspected arson attack outside a defence-technology firm in Munich, days after two sabotage attempts on the power grid and a month after the Leipzig airport drone attack. No attribution has been made for the Munich fire.
Denmark's national security and intelligence service PET says Russia is recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage against Danish defence companies with ties to Ukraine.

President Donald Trump says the United States will seek back payment from European governments for aid provided to Ukraine. He gives no figure, mechanism or timeframe; European capitals have not responded publicly.
Ukrainian authorities say an overnight Russian attack on Kyiv injured 10 people, started a fire and damaged a high-rise building. The account is Ukrainian and has not been independently verified.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russian drones struck a Coca-Cola bottling plant outside Kyiv. Moscow says it targets military and military-industrial sites; the claim is not independently verified.
Zelensky says he expects to host US envoys in Kyiv in the 'coming days'. Neither side has named the officials or set a date.
Zelensky says an investigation is under way after a clash between two Ukrainian security agencies, without naming the bodies involved.

Russia demands the 'immediate release' of the research vessel Professor Molchanov, seized by Norway off Svalbard to enforce a US$4.22 billion arbitration award won by Ukraine's Naftogaz. Moscow calls the seizure piracy; Oslo says it is enforcing a court award.
A Russian court imposes restrictions on the head of a children's hospice charged over posts about the war, the latest in a run of prosecutions over wartime speech.

German police respond to two more suspected attacks on the electricity grid, Bild reports: an attempt to short-circuit a grid installation in Dormagen, where a letter claiming responsibility was received, and a cordoned-off transformer station in Ganderkesee. A police spokesperson told NDR an overnight discovery prompted the response and there was no danger to the public. The incidents are unattributed; Berlin has separately blamed Russia for last month's Leipzig airport drone attempt, which Moscow denies.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Bild, NDR, German police)

timeline.event: Finland's Border Guard says it is investigating whether a surveillance drone found on the shore of its southern coast violated Finnish territory. A preliminary examination identifies it as a Geoscan 701, a survey and mapping model used by both state and civilian operators. The Border Guard says it cannot confirm the drone's origin, operator or purpose; the defence ministry says it posed no danger to the public.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Finnish Border Guard, Finnish defence ministry)

timeline.event: WHO says a warehouse storing medical supplies in the Kyiv region was attacked overnight. The agency has not attributed the strike beyond describing it as part of the ongoing attacks on Ukraine.

Russian state agency TASS reports that envoys of President Donald Trump will visit Russia and Ukraine at the weekend. The Kremlin declined to comment and Washington has not confirmed the trip; the report is a Russian state-media claim.

A BBC survey of August incidents describes a spiralling sabotage campaign against European defence and military sites - fires at Bulgaria's EMCO plant on 10 August, at KNDS Ammo Italy outside Rome on 13 August and at Estonia's Milrem Robotics in Tallinn on 15 August, where two suspects were arrested - following the discovery of explosive-laden drones at Leipzig airport on 4 August. Germany's interior minister says 'Russia is responsible' for the Leipzig attack; the Kremlin calls the accusation 'absurd' and demands proof. Some fires remain under investigation and may yet be ruled accidental.
timeline.source: BBC (German interior ministry, Polish interior minister Marcin Kierwinski, Kremlin, La Repubblica, Kyiv Post)

timeline.event: A Russian drone strikes the Kyiv headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service, one of the most high-profile targets hit in more than four years of war. Kyiv's mayor says at least 12 people are wounded. President Volodymyr Zelensky says the drone was aimed directly at the office of the SBU's head and that he has ordered a response that will 'mirror' the strike; SBU head Oleksandr Poklad briefed him on preparations. It is the 10th consecutive day of Russian air attacks on the capital. Moscow has not publicly commented on the target and the Ukrainian account has not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC, CNA (Volodymyr Zelensky, Kyiv city authorities)

timeline.event: A senior Ukrainian official says there is growing appetite among partners for negotiations on the use of frozen Russian assets. No decision or mechanism has been agreed and the characterisation is Kyiv's.

German police respond to a third suspected sabotage attempt against the electricity grid as a state election approaches. German officials have blamed Russia for some recent incidents; the Kremlin calls the accusations absurd and investigators have not ruled out other causes in every case.
The Kremlin says the position President Vladimir Putin set out two years ago - that Ukraine should cede the whole of four regions Russia claims and abandon its bid to join NATO - is 'unshakeable'.

President Donald Trump says his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are travelling abroad over the weekend to discuss a Ukraine peace settlement, confirming trips to Moscow and Kyiv that Russian state agency TASS had trailed a day earlier and the Kremlin had declined to comment on. No agenda or meeting list has been published.

Zelensky says he will meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Sunday, after the pair meet President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. Trump says the envoys are 'bringing with them a proposal to end the war'; no terms have been made public and the two sides remain far apart.

Oleksandr Ganzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration, says four people were killed and five wounded in a Russian strike on the south-eastern city of Kamianske. Russia has not commented.

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner land in Moscow and are met by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev, two people familiar with the visit tell Reuters. Dmitriev took part in all their previous meetings with Putin. Zelensky says the pair will fly to Ukraine on 6 September.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (sources familiar with the visit)

timeline.event: Zelensky says in a post on X that Russia struck two Ukrainian airports ahead of the US envoys' visit to Kyiv. The claim is Ukraine's and has not been independently confirmed; Russia has not commented.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: The war has come to Iran's oil terminal. Tasnim reported on 5 September that a tanker at the Kharg Island anchorage was hit by four US missiles, with no casualties and the crew evacuated; neither Tehran nor US Central Command has confirmed it, and Trump had posted on 31 August that Kharg was being 'blown to smithereens'. The pressure track is otherwise financial and diplomatic: Washington sanctioned an Istanbul investment bank and two subsidiaries - the first bank in a NATO ally hit under this campaign - while the US, Britain, France and Germany push the IAEA board to refer Iran to the Security Council for the first time in about 20 years, with inspectors still barred from the bombed enrichment sites. Trump called the conflict 'small potatoes' on 5 September. Casualty and strike claims come from parties to the conflict.

timeline.event: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the coming sanctions will be the toughest in history, will 'squash' Iran's economy and that Washington intends to 'collapse this regime', suggesting the move lessens the need for new major military operations. No details of the measures have been released.
The BBC reports that Iran has for years proved adept at working around punishing sanctions, raising doubts about how much the threatened measures would bite.
The US Treasury issues fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, including re-designating it under a terrorism authority, in a move framed around the group's links to the Iranian government.
A new US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been on station for an extended deployment.
Yemen's Houthis say they targeted a Saudi airport and a Saudi Aramco facility. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any damage and the claim is not independently verified.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war: 'It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.' It is the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership that Tehran wants an exit, and follows its foreign ministry accusing Washington of 'economic terrorism'.

The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, says Tehran will answer new US threats with 'crushing, punishing and devastating responses' across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Washington appears to have concluded it cannot prevail militarily.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says details of the threatened sanctions package will be published on Aug 24, after saying the measures will be the toughest in history and are intended to collapse the Iranian government.
China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not resolve the conflict and urges a political solution, rebuffing Washington's request that Beijing help isolate Iran's economy.
A teenager pleads guilty in London over an arson attack on the offices of the Persian-language broadcaster Iran International.

NATO's supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate possible contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. His spokesperson stresses it is not a NATO mission; France and Britain have been assembling a coalition of about a dozen countries to guarantee safe passage, which would ultimately need Iranian acquiescence.

President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity' - the clearest exit signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership, delivered as Washington prepares to publish its sanctions package on Aug 24.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the imminent US sanctions package an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations' with 'no foundation in international law'. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the measures at a press conference at 2pm EDT on Monday and is pressing Beijing to cooperate; China, which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil on 2025 Kpler data, has urged diplomacy instead. The two sides are neither exchanging fire nor holding talks.

Ship-tracking data shows only four commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 20, none of them large crude or LNG carriers, with thousands of seafarers stranded on hundreds of vessels. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the US military helped move a seven-day average of 8 million barrels a day through the strait, against more than 20 million a day before the war.

Iran grants permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, state news agency IRNA reports. Iraqi President Nizar Amedi says passage has been facilitated in recent days but calls the issue complicated. Traffic remains far below pre-war levels and ships continue to face attacks.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (IRNA, Iraqi President Nizar Amedi)

timeline.event: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent schedules a 2pm EDT Monday press conference to unveil the sanctions package, having promised 'the toughest sanctions in history' and urged Beijing to cooperate. China buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler, and has urged diplomacy.
Two US tanker aircraft leave Bulgaria's Bezmer air base, the Bulgarian defence minister says, nearly a month after their deployment angered Tehran.
An Iranian official urges Qatar to move detained pilots from a vessel to a hospital on land.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei denounces the US plan to announce new sanctions, calling it an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty' over other states. CNA notes that after nearly six months since the US and Israel began strikes on Feb 28, the sides are not firing at each other but show no sign of peace talks, and that oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are at a virtual standstill.

Mohsen Rezai, head of Iran's supreme national security council, warns on state television that any country joining the US 'economic war' will be 'considered an enemy'. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the package on Monday; China, which buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil according to 2025 Kpler data, has urged diplomacy.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Iranian state television)

timeline.event: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi dismisses the threatened US sanctions as 'repetitive scenarios' and a sign of desperation, saying they will fail to defeat Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the package at a 2pm EDT press conference on Monday, having promised 'the toughest sanctions in history'.

Iran executes a man it accused of aiding the United States and Israel during anti-government protests. The charges and the trial process are Iranian state accounts and have not been independently verified.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent writes in the Financial Times that 'at dawn begins an economic D-Day - the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary', trailing sanctions aimed at Iran's trading partners.

Iran says it has discovered a gas field holding more than 200 billion cubic metres, after the war damaged its energy sector. The claim comes from Iranian officials and has not been independently verified.

Iran vows to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf 'if the economic war continues', and warns that any country supporting the US sanctions will be treated as taking a hostile act. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is already near a standstill.

Oil prices fall as traders weigh the scale of the threatened US sanctions against the prospect of Iranian retaliation. Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 1pm EDT on 24 Aug (1am on 25 Aug Singapore time).

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington will sever all economic ties with Iran in 'an economic D-Day', calling it 'the single greatest financial offensive ever' and claiming the war is 'entering its endgame'. Writing in the Financial Times, he says any nation partnering with Iran financially will also be isolated, but gives no detail on the measures; he is due to set them out at a press conference at 1pm US Eastern time (1am Singapore time on 25 August).

Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi mocks the threat as an admission of American defeat, arguing on X that Washington cannot simultaneously claim Iran's military and nuclear capabilities were destroyed and that the largest financial offensive in history is still needed.

Iran's newly created Persian Gulf Strait Authority warns that vessels breaching its Strait of Hormuz transit arrangements face restrictions including fines, detention or confiscation, and says ships doing ship-to-ship transfers with non-compliant vessels will themselves be added to a restricted list.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Persian Gulf Strait Authority)

timeline.event: Pakistan's army chief flies to Tehran on a mediating mission as the US prepares the sanctions package. Pakistan previously brokered a de-escalation after Trump's April ultimatum.
South Korea says the United States has cancelled a joint marine exercise because of the Iran war, the latest sign of US forces being redirected towards the Gulf.
Iran says it has found a new gas field, which officials present as a cushion after the war damaged its energy sector.

Oil transits through the Strait of Hormuz ran at five million barrels per day, provisional data from shiptracker Vortexa showed, against more than 20 million per day before the war — about one in every five barrels consumed worldwide.

At a Washington press conference on Monday branded 'Operation Economic Outcast', US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions determinations against five Iranian sectors — digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping — plus measures against almost 60 entities, individuals and vessels. He called it 'the single greatest financial offensive ever' and said America was 'no longer managing the Iranian threat, we are ending it'.

Iran's economy minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran has a two-year plan to counter the sanctions and that they would end in another defeat for Washington. Iran repeated that it would shut down all oil exports from the region if the war continues.

Analysts noted the package stopped short of the harshest options the White House had threatened. Oil prices fell as traders read the announcement as more moderate than the 'economic D-Day' language suggested.
Pakistan's army chief met Iran's president in Tehran, continuing Islamabad's mediation effort as the sanctions package landed.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Iran had 'tried to kill' one of his sons. The claim has not been independently verified and Iran has not commented publicly on it.

Iran's economy minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran was 'fully prepared' for the new sanctions and predicted 'another defeat' for Washington, telling state television that neither China nor Russia had accepted the measures and that other countries would resist them. The UAE, one of Iran's largest trading partners alongside China and Turkey, announced last week it was halting all trade and financial transactions with Tehran.

The International Maritime Organization confirmed 68 maritime incidents in the Gulf and neighbouring waters over the six months of the war, in which at least 20 workers were killed, 35 wounded and one is missing, mostly on tankers. The rate slowed to no casualties during the peace talks and returned to roughly one incident every 2.8 days after they collapsed.

Pakistan's interior minister said talks in Tehran had made 'significant progress', with Pakistan's military saying the meetings between army chief Asim Munir and the Iranian leadership covered preventing further escalation, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and expediting an end to the conflict. The characterisation is Islamabad's; Tehran has not issued a matching statement and no terms have been published.

The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control named Singapore-based Wellbred Capital, with trading arms in the UAE and Switzerland, among close to 60 companies, individuals and vessels designated over Iran links, citing ties to Iranian oil shipping figure Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said Beijing's cooperation with Iran is conducted within the framework of international law and 'should not be interfered with or disrupted', and that China would take 'all necessary measures' to safeguard its rights and interests after Washington widened sanctions.

The New York Times reported, citing an internal State Department document, that Washington is preparing to return Foreign Service officers to Middle East embassies evacuated before and during the war, including in Israel, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Oman, Iraq and Kuwait, possibly from this week. The report is not independently verified; the department said it 'continuously reviews' its security posture.
Long queues formed at petrol stations in Tehran after Washington announced fresh sanctions, a day after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent set out plans for the 'economic asphyxiation' of Iran.
Iran and Oman said they had discussed opening a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz along with mine-clearing work. No timetable or mechanism was announced.

President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that all mines had been detonated or removed from international waters in the Strait of Hormuz, that the US Space Force was watching 'every square inch', and that Iran had been told any vessel placing new mines would be destroyed. Iran has not confirmed the account.
The US Secret Service said it was aware of an Iranian video threat against Barron Trump, the president's son. The service did not describe the threat as credible.
China's foreign ministry called the widened US sanctions on Iran and its trading partners 'illegal', with spokesperson Lin Jian saying Beijing's cooperation with Tehran should not be disrupted.
Oil prices fell as traders weighed the threat of wider US sanctions on Iran and its trading partners, suggesting markets are not pricing an immediate supply shock.

Iran and Oman said they had discussed opening a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz together with mine-clearing work, as the impasse with Washington drags on. Neither government gave a timeline and the account has not been independently verified.
Ship-tracking data showed Gulf traffic through the Strait of Hormuz still running below its 10-day average, despite President Donald Trump's statement that the waterway had been cleared of mines.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said no diplomatic deal was possible with Iran, calling its leadership 'savages'. Tehran has not responded to the remark.
Gulf air hubs are absorbing a wartime downturn in traffic, with carriers and airports reporting reduced volumes through the conflict.
A senior Iranian source said Iran and Oman are still working on an accord covering shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. No timetable or mechanism has been given by either government.
Qatar's prime minister will travel to Tehran to pursue mediation efforts, adding a second Gulf channel alongside Oman's.

Allied officials privately assess that the Strait of Hormuz is still likely mined, saying demining has not cleared all of the estimated 80 to 150 mines laid by Iran and that sea currents have moved many of them from their original positions. The assessment challenges President Donald Trump's repeated statement that the strait is clear; US Central Command declined to comment. Iran has opposed foreign mine-clearing operations in the strait.
Qatar's prime minister travelled to Tehran to pursue mediation efforts, opening a second Gulf channel alongside Oman's talks with Iran.

Six months after US and Israeli forces attacked Iran on 28 February, The Straits Times assessed the war as a costly stalemate: Washington's sanctions package announced on 24 August shifts the fight from missiles to Iran's oil revenues, banks and trading partners, while a US-led naval blockade restricts its exports. Tehran is betting that Washington will not aggressively enforce secondary sanctions on China and India.
A Greek-operated air defence system shot down drones over Saudi Arabia.
The White House said there are no negotiations under way with Iran and that all options remain on the table.

President Donald Trump said the United States is not talking to Iran, with the confrontation now focused on economic pressure, and vowed to penalise countries that continue doing business with Tehran. Qatar's prime minister meanwhile pressed on with mediation in Tehran.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (White House, Qatari government)

timeline.event: Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei set out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and said Iran had agreed with Oman on a shipping corridor through the strait. Washington has not confirmed any such arrangement.

A senior US Treasury official said the US-hosted G20 finance meeting next week will press members to cut off Iran's economic lifelines, alongside talks on growth, global imbalances and sovereign debt.

Mediation shifted decisively to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar's prime minister met senior Iranian leaders in Tehran on 27 August and pressed for a return to pre-war freedom of navigation, after which Tehran agreed to draw up a list of conditions for restoring normal traffic. Iran's conditions are reported to include sanctions relief, which Washington has not accepted; the US has disengaged from talks in favour of economic pressure.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Qatari and Iranian officials)

timeline.event: The Straits Times reported that Iran's supreme leader has remained out of public view six months into the war, with no verified public appearance since the opening strikes.
Qatar formally stepped in as mediator between Washington and Tehran, CNA reported, after Trump said the United States is not talking to Iran and is relying on economic pressure instead.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Qatari government, White House)

timeline.event: The US Treasury moved to cut the UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr off from dollar transactions over their dealings with Iran, as the war marked six months.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said diplomacy remains possible if Washington abandons its pressure campaign, six months into the war.
Iran publicly condemned the latest round of US sanctions as its own economy came under mounting strain.
The BBC reported that the Trump administration plans to cut off military aid to Iraqi Kurdistan, whose officials say the move would leave the region more exposed to further Iranian attacks.
The Straits Times reported that the war is weighing heavily on Iran's economy as Washington intensifies sanctions, with Tehran publicly rejecting the latest measures.

The BBC reported that piracy off Somalia has surged as an indirect effect of the war, with two ships seized within four days last week and at least 13 vessels attacked since January as naval attention and commercial traffic shifted.

Iran's leadership is due at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan alongside the Russian and Chinese leaders, its most visible multilateral appearance since the sanctions escalation.
Iran says it remains open to diplomacy as the war with the United States reaches six months, while hitting out at the latest US sanctions and the economic toll at home.

The US Treasury issues a notice cutting the UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr off from dollar transactions over dealings with Iran. The bank says it is reviewing the notice and that its UAE branch still serves customers; the UAE central bank orders a "special and urgent examination" of those branches, including a forensic look-back over the period Washington cited.

The BBC reports, citing four sources familiar with the talks, that the US Department of Defense has told leaders of Iraq's Kurdistan region that Washington does not plan to renew the expiring security-assistance agreement funding the Peshmerga. Kurdish officials say the cut would create a vacuum and embolden Iran, which they say has fired hundreds of missiles and drones into Iraqi Kurdistan since the war began. The Pentagon has not confirmed the plan publicly.

Piracy off Somalia reaches its highest level in more than a decade, with two cargo vessels seized in the Gulf of Aden within four days and at least 13 ships attacked this year, prompting unprecedented drone strikes on the pirates. Analysts link the surge to the contested Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis' targeted blockade at the Bab al-Mandab.

Republican strategists say they see no way to keep the war from damaging the party in November's midterms, with polling cited by The Straits Times showing 63 per cent disapprove of President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict and his overall approval at 33 per cent amid high petrol prices.

The UAE's central bank launches an urgent forensic examination of Banque Misr's operations in the country after the US Treasury notice restricting the Egyptian bank's UAE branches from dollar transactions over dealings with Iran. Banque Misr says it is reviewing the notice.

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei publishes a message for Islamic Unity Week urging Muslim countries, and Gulf states in particular, to unite against what he calls their 'real enemy' and to cooperate on mutual defence. He has not appeared in public since being injured in the US-Israeli strikes six months ago that killed his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan will hold the first committee meeting under their Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in Istanbul on 31 August, a Turkish foreign ministry source says. The 7 August pact treats an attack on one as an attack on all and was signed by Sunni Muslim US allies unsettled by the Iran war and Iranian missile fire on Gulf oil exporters.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, Turkish foreign ministry source)

timeline.event: US forces strike two Iranian launchers on Larak Island, off Bandar Abbas in the Strait of Hormuz - the first known American strikes on Iran since late July. US Central Command spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins said IRGC forces "were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into Strait of Hormuz".
timeline.source: BBC (US Central Command via CBS News), The Straits Times, CNA

timeline.event: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the Larak Island strike killed and wounded several soldiers and civilians and vow "response and punishment"; Iranian state media then say Iran has attacked US military targets in Jordan. Iranian claims, not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC (Iranian state media, IRGC), The Straits Times

timeline.event: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the department will likely announce new secondary sanctions on Iran every week, starting with banks, and that the next step may be cutting an institution off from the dollar system entirely.

Jordan's armed forces say air defences intercepted eight missiles that breached the kingdom's airspace at dawn, quoting the army spokesperson via the state Petra news agency. A Fox News reporter, citing a US source, said nearly all incoming missiles had been intercepted with no significant impact.
timeline.source: BBC (Jordanian armed forces via Petra), The Straits Times

timeline.event: The UAE says it will investigate a Banque Misr branch after the US cited Iran links, The Straits Times reports, following the US Treasury notice restricting the Egyptian bank's UAE operations.

Iranian media carry an IRGC statement saying it struck the US bases of King Hussein and al-Azraq in Jordan with ballistic missiles in response to the Larak Island attack; Iran's foreign ministry calls the strikes "legitimate defence" and President Masoud Pezeshkian says Iran is "not seeking war" but will deliver a decisive response. Claims by a party to the conflict.
timeline.source: BBC (IRGC, Iranian foreign ministry, Iranian state TV)

timeline.event: Iran's army says it attacked the UAE's Al Minhad Air Base with drones early on Monday, targeting locations where US forces and helicopters are stationed, in response to the killing of Revolutionary Guards and civilians on Larak Island; the UAE says it shot down a drone. Iranian state TV claim.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian state TV), BBC (UAE)

timeline.event: Trump posts apparent AI-generated videos on Truth Social showing oil infrastructure exploding, one captioned "Kharg Island being blown to smithereens!!!"; there is no evidence of an actual attack on Iran's main oil export terminal.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards say a supertanker attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz "illegally" was struck by two mines and caught fire. IRGC claim, not independently verified; Washington said last week that all Iranian mines in the strait had been detonated or removed.
US Central Command says it disabled three vessels, boarded two and redirected 82 as part of the continuing naval blockade of Iran, the BBC reports.

The UAE's defence ministry rejects as "unfounded" Iranian state TV reports that Al Minhad Air Base was targeted, while confirming the UAE shot down a drone. Iran's army says it attacked the base with drones in response to the killing of Revolutionary Guards and civilians. Both accounts are claims by parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: BBC (UAE Ministry of Defence), The Straits Times (Iranian state TV)

timeline.event: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says Iran still wants a negotiated end to the war, speaking after the exchanges of fire. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says he expects new US secondary sanctions to be announced weekly to increase pressure on Tehran.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian presidency, US Treasury)

timeline.event: Xi Jinping and Pezeshkian arrive in Kyrgyzstan for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, with Vladimir Putin also expected — putting the leaders of Iran, Russia and China in one room days after the latest US-Iran exchange.

CNA publishes an assessment more than six months into the conflict, reporting that neither side has achieved its stated objectives while US financial and military costs continue to mount. Analysis, not a new development.

Iranian state media, citing the Revolutionary Guards, says a supertanker caught fire and was brought to a complete halt after striking two naval mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz. The Guards said the vessel had been trying to transit “illegally” and warned other ships breaking its rules would face the same fate, without naming the vessel or commenting on its crew. Claim by a party to the conflict, not independently verified.

Iranian state media says three people were killed and several wounded in Sunday's US strike on Larak Island — a higher toll than the two deaths the IRGC initially reported. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say their ballistic missile attack on two US air bases in Jordan caused “heavy damage”. All casualty and damage claims come from parties to the conflict.

President Donald Trump says of Iran: “We're going to hit them hard. There will be a response,” according to a Fox News reporter. Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed and the US maintains its counter-blockade of Iranian ports, six months into the war.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, speaking at the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, says Tehran still wants a negotiated end: “we believe that continuing the war is neither in our interest, nor in the interest of the region”, adding that “the solution to the existing problems is dialogue and cooperation”.

Iran seizes a sugar-carrying bulk carrier that authorities say dumped burnt oil, bilge water and industrial sludge into the Strait of Hormuz, referring it to the judiciary. Hormozgan ports official Esmaeil Makizadeh gave no flag or crew nationality. Iran has demanded compensation for several recent oil spills and says it plans to charge transit fees to fund services including environmental protection — fees the United States fiercely opposes.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (IRNA, Hormozgan Ports and Maritime Department)

timeline.event: Oil settles more than 2.5 per cent higher on the resumption of fighting: Brent up US$2.39 to US$90.49 a barrel and WTI up 2.83 per cent to US$85.76, with Brent touching US$91.52 intraday, its highest since 25 August. Shipping data showed visible commodity vessels transiting Hormuz fell to five a day over the weekend, against about a fifth of global oil supply before the war. Mediation on reopening the strait has stalled.
timeline.source: CNA (ICE and NYMEX settlement data, shipping data)

timeline.event: Oil prices extend their gains and Asian equity markets fall on fears of renewed US-Iran military exchanges after the weekend flare-up and President Donald Trump's warning that he will hit Iran 'hard'. Tokyo, Hong Kong, Seoul, Shanghai, Sydney and Singapore all trade lower. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed by Tehran while Washington continues its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran's central bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati says Iran has sufficient foreign currency reserves despite US sanctions and that the bank is ready to inject up to US$2 billion into the foreign exchange market to calm volatility, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. 'I am telling the President of the United States: Iran has (foreign) currency and it has enough,' he said. The remarks follow US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's claim that Tehran is lashing out because it is losing the economic war, and come after Iranian officials including President Masoud Pezeshkian pointed to growing economic difficulty. Hemmati's figures are the Iranian central bank's own and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Tasnim, Central Bank of Iran)

timeline.event: Iran says it will reciprocate if the United States honours its commitments under the June interim deal. A senior Iranian source describes the recent exchanges of fire as a “limited and contained confrontation” but says Tehran would respond harshly to any further attack; President Donald Trump, quoted by a Fox News reporter as saying “we're going to hit them hard”, separately told reporters the strikes did not signal a return to full-scale war. Neither account has been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian presidency, senior Iranian source, Fox News quoting Trump)

timeline.event: US Central Command says American forces resumed strikes on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets from 12:00 US Eastern time on Tuesday, citing 'recent attempted attacks' by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian Red Crescent says shrapnel from a US missile hit a house where a wedding was being held in Sirik in southern Iran, killing four people - Iranian state media says a four-year-old child was among them - and wounding more than 50. Iranian reports also describe projectiles hitting Chabahar, Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, with explosions heard on Qeshm island and in Bandar Abbas. Casualty and damage claims are from parties to the fighting and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA (US Central Command, Iranian Red Crescent, Iranian state media)

timeline.event: President Donald Trump, as the US strikes were announced, warns that Iran will be hit at 'a much harder and higher level' if it retaliates.

Iran launches a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Aqaba, Jordan, in retaliation for the Sirik strike, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, and attacks US bases in Iraq. The Jordanian Armed Forces say they intercepted 13 ballistic missiles, destroying 10, with three falling in remote areas and no deaths or injuries; Jordan's national security centre warned residents of the Aqaba and Mafraq governorates about falling debris. Kuwait's army says its air defences responded to Iranian missile attacks, and Iranian state media report several explosions in Bahrain. The IRGC says the US will 'regret' the strikes.
timeline.source: BBC (Jordanian Armed Forces, Kuwaiti army, Tasnim, IRGC)

timeline.event: Oil settles more than US$4 a barrel higher on the renewed US-Iran fighting. Iran's parliament speaker urges Iranians to cut petrol use, and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington plans to increase economic sanctions on Iran and has discussed further action with allies as well as Russia and China.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (settlement data, Iranian parliament, US Treasury)

timeline.event: The United Nations faces a contentious vote on Iran's nuclear programme ahead of the General Assembly, The Straits Times reports.

The Iranian Red Crescent raises the toll from the US strike on Sirik, on the Strait of Hormuz, to five killed - including a child - and more than 50 injured, saying shrapnel from a US missile hit a house where a wedding was being held. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, for Centcom, says the US is aware of the reports and that 'the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC'.
timeline.source: BBC (Iranian Red Crescent, US Central Command)

timeline.event: The IRGC fires missiles and drones at US targets in Jordan, Kuwait, Iraq and Bahrain. Jordan's armed forces say they intercepted 13 ballistic missiles, destroying 10, with three falling in remote areas and no deaths or injuries; Kuwait's army says its air defences responded; Iranian state media report explosions in Bahrain and IRNA says the IRGC destroyed a maintenance centre, warehouses and equipment at US bases in Iraq's Kurdistan region. All figures are the claims of parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: BBC (Jordanian Armed Forces, Kuwait army, IRNA, Tasnim, IRGC)

timeline.event: Centcom says its latest wave of strikes on IRGC targets began at 12:00 US Eastern time and was completed by early Wednesday, citing recent attempted IRGC attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on American forces. Iranian state media report projectiles hit Chabahar, Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, with explosions heard on Qeshm island and in Bandar Abbas.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (US Central Command, Iranian state media)

timeline.event: Crude rises more than 2 per cent and is up about 10 per cent on the week, with the Strait of Hormuz - about a fifth of world oil and gas traffic - effectively closed. Bond yields hold at multi-decade highs, 30-year UK gilts at their highest since 1998, and traders price in roughly a 70 per cent chance of a US Federal Reserve rate hike, according to Bloomberg.
timeline.source: CNA (ICE/NYMEX settlement data, Bloomberg, Gama Asset Management)

timeline.event: A car strikes a gathering of supporters of Iran's government and armed forces in the north-eastern city of Mashhad overnight, killing four people and injuring more than 10, several Iranian media report. The circumstances have not been independently confirmed.

Iran says at least 12 people were killed in the latest US strikes, five of them at a wedding at a home in Sirik on the coast of the Strait of Hormuz, including a four-year-old. Iranian media put the wounded there at as many as 68 and published images of injured children. The figures are Iranian official and state-linked accounts and are not independently verified.

Qatar, host of the largest US air base in the Gulf, says it holds Iran fully legally responsible for the attacks and their consequences; Bahrain, which houses the US Navy's regional headquarters, says Iranian drones were intercepted and destroyed.
Iran says two tankers were struck by mines while being steered across the Strait of Hormuz by US vessels through a channel Tehran says it has closed. The claim has not been independently confirmed.
Saudi shipping company Bahri says two of its sailors were killed in an incident involving one of its oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on 31 August.
Aides to President Donald Trump, worried about a midterm rout, are pressing to keep the Iran war 'quiet' for now, The Straits Times reports.
Iran urges the United States to comply with the interim deal after Trump threatens further strikes.

Iran's health minister says 18 people were killed and 108 injured in Tuesday's US strikes, revising up an earlier figure of at least 12. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei calls a strike that hit a wedding at a home in Sirik a 'war crime'; the Iranian Red Crescent says shrapnel killed four people there, including two children. A Centcom spokesperson says the US 'never targets civilians' and is aware of the reports. Iranian authorities say another 14 people were killed elsewhere. None of the figures are independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC (Iranian health ministry, Iranian Red Crescent Society, Esmaeil Baqaei, US Central Command)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia condemns what it says was an Iranian attack on the Bahri-owned supertanker Sidr in the Strait of Hormuz at about 23:40 local time on Monday. Bahri confirms two Filipino seafarers were killed. Maritime security firms say Sidr was hit by projectiles north of Oman's Musandam Peninsula and that the South Korean-owned Senegal Prosperity was struck east of Musandam around the same time. Iran has not responded to the allegation, but said earlier that two tankers caught fire after striking mines on an unauthorised route.
timeline.source: BBC (Saudi government, Bahri, maritime security firms)

timeline.event: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warns that operations against American forces in the region will continue until the US 'regrets' its actions.
Israel says it is prepared to 'respond with great force' if Iran attacks, with forces readied for a possible attack over the Jewish high holiday season beginning in mid-September.
President Donald Trump floats renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait', after claiming US sovereignty over the waterway Tehran has effectively shut for six months.

Iran attacks US military bases in Kuwait. Kuwait's army says it is intercepting a missile and drone attack; Iranian state TV says the strikes target US bases in the Gulf state 'in response to America's crimes against the Iranian people'. Tehran says it also hit US targets in Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq's Kurdistan region. Trump says the US is prepared to attack Iran 'any time we want'; security chief Mohsen Rezaei says Iran has adopted a 'new strategy' that 'will shatter your foundations'. All strike and interception claims are from parties to the war.
timeline.source: CNA (Kuwait's army, Iranian state TV, Donald Trump, Mohsen Rezaei)

timeline.event: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres says he is 'deeply alarmed by reports of civilian casualties, including a strike that reportedly hit a wedding ceremony in Iran'.

On his first Middle East visit in four years, Chinese President Xi Jinping tells Egypt's Abdel Fattah al-Sisi that regional countries should be 'masters of their own destiny' and explore a new regional 'security architecture', according to Chinese state agency Xinhua. The two agree to deepen security and counter-terrorism cooperation. Egypt receives about US$1.3 billion a year in US military aid.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says Washington will expand sanctions on Iran's trade partners to choke its economy, as the US presses a counter-blockade of Iranian ports while Tehran keeps its hold on the Strait of Hormuz.
The number of Iranian military personnel reported killed by US strikes this week rises to 13, according to Iranian accounts. The figure is Tehran's and is not independently verified.
US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick apologises for saying no Americans have died in the Iran war.

Vice-President J.D. Vance says the United States is investigating whether an American munition struck a wedding party in Iran. The Straits Times reports that open-source analysis points to a likely direct hit by a US munition; the Pentagon has not confirmed a cause, and Iran's casualty account has not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (J.D. Vance, Iranian officials)

timeline.event: Vance says the Iran conflict 'is not a war' and declines to offer a timeline for its end.

South Korea's presidential office says it is reviewing options, including military measures, to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, while denying reports by JTBC and MBC that a deployment had already been decided. Options reported under consideration include a maritime patrol aircraft, a logistics support vessel or a mine-clearance unit. 'Nothing has been decided,' a presidential official said, citing domestic legal procedures, readiness on the Korean Peninsula and the need for parliamentary approval.
timeline.source: CNA (South Korean presidential office, JTBC, MBC)

timeline.event: Three senior Iranian sources tell CNA and The Straits Times that the US effort to blockade Iran's oil exports and cut its access to international financing networks is becoming increasingly difficult to withstand, leaving Tehran with few channels for foreign currency or imports. The assessment comes from Iranian officials and is not independently verified; Iran has warned it could answer the pressure with military escalation.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (senior Iranian sources)

timeline.event: Fighting between Yemen's Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces kills 81 people, military and medical sources tell AFP, as the rebels push towards high ground overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait and the government-held port of Mokha. A coastal military official reported 24 of his men killed and a Taiz official 15; medical sources in Houthi-held areas counted at least 42 rebel dead. All tallies come from parties to the fighting. Bab el-Mandeb has become a critical oil transit route since Iran's blockade of Hormuz.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP, Yemeni military and medical sources)

timeline.event: The US military has switched off advertising trackers on service members' devices after reports that location data broadcast by mobile apps was being used to target American forces in the Middle East.

The United States, Britain, France and Germany seek a resolution at the IAEA's 35-nation board next week referring Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in about 20 years, according to diplomats and a draft text described by news agencies. Iran has not let inspectors return to the enrichment sites destroyed or damaged in the US and Israeli strikes, or verify stocks enriched to up to 60 per cent purity. The draft has not been formally submitted and wording is still being negotiated.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (diplomats, draft IAEA resolution)

timeline.event: The United States sanctions a Turkish bank and two of its subsidiaries in the latest round of Iran-related financial pressure.
US diesel prices reach an all-time high, a knock-on from the disruption to crude and refined-product flows caused by the conflict.

President Donald Trump describes the Iran conflict as 'small potatoes' and plays down the scale of the war, days after Vice-President J.D. Vance declined to call the six-month confrontation a war or set an end date.

Iran's semi-official Tasnim agency reports that a tanker at the Kharg Island anchorage was hit by four US missiles, with no casualties and the crew evacuated. Iranian authorities issue no official statement and US Central Command does not respond to requests for comment, so the account rests on a single state-linked source.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Tasnim news agency)

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Lebanon remains the shooting edge and Gaza the political one. Lebanon's health ministry says Israeli strikes across the south on 4 September killed three people and wounded 23, including medics, women and children; Israel says it struck after Hezbollah launched a drone towards its soldiers, and Hezbollah has not commented.
